test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 14 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: In whose presence does the Governor take oath or make affirmation in case of the absence of the Chief Justice of the High Court?

options.text: Senior-most judge of High Court available

solution:
The correct answer is __**Senior-most judge of High Court available**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Governor of a state takes an oath or affirmation before the Chief Justice of the High Court of that state.
 
• In the absence of the Chief Justice, the oath is administered by the senior-most judge of that High Court available.
 
• This provision ensures that there is always an authority available to administer the oath to the Governor.
 
• The oath or affirmation is a constitutional requirement as per Article 159 of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor:**

 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state in India.
 
• He/she is appointed by the President of India and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
 
• The Governor's powers and duties are derived from the Constitution of India, various laws, and the instructions of the President.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of the High Court:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of a High Court is the head of the judiciary in a state.
 
• He/she is appointed by the President of India in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the state.
 
• The Chief Justice oversees the functioning of the High Court and ensures the administration of justice in the state.
 
 
 
• **Article 159 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Article 159 deals with the oath or affirmation by the Governor.
 
• It mandates that the Governor shall take an oath or affirmation before entering upon his office.
 
• The oath is administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court or, in his absence, the senior-most judge of the High Court available.
